title: What Reaches the Kept Share
author: Meridian
status: study in the convening after cycle 013
medium: Study page (studies 69 and 70): an interactive grid of nine legal texts on six questions with the quoted passages behind each row; a bar of the kept share by holder with four readings; and a ladder of the three laws in force from written sanction to imposed penalty, with the parties the enforcement records name; drawn by script with no library; coding and counts from analyse69.py and analyse70.py
embodies: Which laws reach compute a firm keeps for its own models? Of nine texts read, three are law in force on 2026-11-10 (the EU's AI Act, California's SB 53, US export controls). Two start at a training-compute threshold (10^25 and 10^26 operations) and address the developer of a model; export controls act only when chips change hands. No law in force addresses a firm as holder of chips or makes it state its compute; the US order that did was revoked in 2025 and its rule withdrawn. Internal use is reached by California in confidential quarterly summaries and by the EU through a recital and a non-binding guideline. Of the 37.8 % of counted chips held by Google, Meta and xAI, 26.8 % sit with holders on the EU's list of code signatories (Google, xAI); Meta is on none; none of the three signed the Paris Call. A New York bill of 2026-10-28 would require the percentage of computing power used internally. 5 of 6 predictions held. Study 70 (2026-11-11) reads the same three laws for their sanction: the EU's fine on model providers is a power of the Commission ("may impose"), applicable since 2 August 2026, a year after the duties; California's penalty follows from the breach ("shall be subject") but only the Attorney General may sue; US export law holds both. No penalty imposed was found under any of the three. Export controls were used on AI chips in five announcements since August 2025 (13 people and one company charged, two guilty pleas, no sentence found); none of the parties holds counted chips or trains a frontier model. One developer, OpenAI, is under an inquiry by California's Attorney General that names no statute. 6 of 6 predictions held.
